ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$10.40 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (RD-2, metered RydeTAXI excess distance), and record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file; no account flag (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0).

segment_findings.reason: Off-route from ≈09:10:20 (1.283625,103.809743), where the driver left the quoted AYE/East Coast corridor, south onto the MCE (09:14:20 1.279653,103.823843; 09:17:20 1.268412,103.822738), rejoining only at 09:26:20 (1.280408,103.8277) — ≈5.5 km of extra MCE loop. No incident on the replaced stretch (traffic.incidents = [], RD-4(a) unmet), CXE band 4 / AYE band 2 are corroborative only and cannot exempt alone (RD-4(b)); empty chat means no rider-named stop (RD-3) and no consent before the detour (RD-5). Driver's rain/AYE claim is unevidenced and disconfirmed by his ~40 km/h sustained speeds. Unexempted → RD-1 breach, refund per RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Claimed AYE was crawling and flooding so the detour was reasonable. traffic.incidents = [] (no incident on the replaced route stretch, RD-4(a) unmet); speed on the abandoned AYE corridor is band 2 (0<9/10<19 km/h range, corroborative only per RD-4(b)) and his own GPS shows sustained 35–44 km/h through 09:09–09:14 and the swept MCE, so the 'crawling/flooding' justification is not supported by system records, which override the statement.
